sample_unit: chest X-ray images (balanced subset of NIH ChestX-ray14, five-fold)

links.outcome: Selective-prediction performance (AURC, error at high coverage) of an agent that abstains on uncertain cases for human review
links.effect: Both AT-CXR routers achieved lower AURC and lower error at high coverage than zero-shot VLMs and supervised classifiers, with higher full-coverage accuracy. No numeric values in the text.
links.quote: Across five-fold evaluation on a balanced subset of NIH ChestX-ray14 dataset, both variants outperform strong zero-shot vision-language models and state-of-the-art supervised classifiers, achieving higher full-coverage accuracy and superior selective-prediction performance, evidenced by a lower area under the risk-coverage curve (AURC) and a lower error rate at high coverage, while operating with lower latency that meets practical clinical constraints.

links.outcome: Whether the agent defers or abstains appropriately on uncertain cases, measured by risk-coverage tradeoffs
links.effect: Uncertainty-aware abstention policy gave lower risk-coverage AUC and lower error at high coverage than baselines. Two routers offer throughput-focused or accuracy-focused operating points. No numeric values in the text.
links.quote: The two routers provide complementary operating points, enabling deployments to prioritize maximal throughput or maximal accuracy.
